5.76.010
Intent-Authority-General provisions.
A. The purpose of this chapter is to establish regulations and procedures for
conducting or soliciting sales and related activities within the city.
B.The city of Cheyenne is authorized by Wyo.Stat. Section 15-1-103(a)(xii) and
Wyo.Stat.Section 33-20-210 to regulate and license the conduct of sales by temporary or transient
merchants and residential door-to-door solicitors for the public health, safety and welfare of its
citizens.

5.76.020
Definitions.
The following definitions shall apply in the interpretation and enforcement of this chapter:
"Applicant" means an individual who is at least eighteen (18) years of age. If an applicant
other lawfully formed entity, the individual must be a designated representative of same.
"Charitable organization" means any association, organization, corporation, partnership,
limited liability company, or lawfully formed entity that is:
1.A benevolent, educational, philanthropic, humane, patriotic, religious, social
welfare, advocacy, public health, environmental, conservation, or civic organization established
for any charitable purpose, and
2.Tax exempt under applicable provisions of the Internal Revenue Code, as amended,
and qualified under federal law to solicit andreceive tax deductible contributions from thepublic
for charitable purposes.
"Comprehensive license” means an annual temporary or transient merchant business
license issued to a permanent organization or business, or to an applicant in conjunction with a
special local temporary event or activity, which allows any number of temporary or transient
merchants to sell or offer for sale retail goods, merchandise or services fromfixed stands, tables,
booths, vehicles or trailers at the location identified on the application, or renewal application,
form.A comprehensive license does not include the sale of food items requiring a separate
license or permit pursuant to Chapter 8.40 of city code.A comprehensive license pertains to sales
activities involving temporary or transient merchants only and not residential door-to-door
solicitors.
"Contribution" or “contributions” means and includes the words alms, food, clothing,
money, property, financial assistance or other things of value.A contribution, as defined herein,
will also include a residential door-to-door solicitor selling or offering to sell any book, card,
magazine, membership, merchandise, subscription, ticket orother thing in connection withwhich
an appeal is made for charitable, educational or religious purposes.
"Door-to-door solicitor” or “solicitors" means any individual, as approved in conjunction
with a residential door-to-door solicitors business license, attempting to make personal contact with
any person at a place of residence within the city, without prior invitation by or appointment with
2
2:
the resident, for the purpose of solicitation or sale of goods, merchandise or services.
"License identification badge”means the identification badge issued bythe city clerk to an
individual approved to conduct door-to-door solicitation activities in conjunction with a residential
door-to-door solicitors business license.Each badge will contain a current photograph of the
individual to whom the badge is assigned.
"No soliciting” or"no solicitation” sign means a reasonably visible and legible sign posted
similar import.
“Permanent place of business” means a recognized, fixed business location within the city
at which the business owner, manager or designated agent actively operates a business which is
open to the public on a year-round basis with regularly established hours of business.A
permanent place of business also includes a location within the city in which a person conducts
business as a home occupation and the person provides goods, merchandise orservices, or delivers
orders for same, to a customer's residence upon the customer's prior request or invitation.
"Religious" means and includes the word “charitable,” as herein defined, but will be given
its commonly accepted definition.
“Residence",“residential"or“residential premises"means any living unit contained within
any building, structure, or manufactured housing unit that is predominantly occupied byanyperson
as a dwelling, together with the lot, or other real property on which the living unit is located.
“Residential door-to-door solicitors business license”means the license issued by the city
clerk in connection with a valid application as outlined in this chapter, and applies only to
solicitation activities involving personal contact with anyperson at aplace of residence within the
city, without prior invitation by or appointment with the resident, for the purpose of solicitation or
sale of goods, merchandise or services.A residential door-to-door solicitors business license is
only valid for a period of fourteen (14) consecutive days beginning on the date of issuance.
"Sale”,“sales", “sell” or“offer for sale” of goods, merchandise or services means any
verbal or written agreement involving a solicitation between a residential door-to-door solicitor and
an adult individual residing within a residence.
"Solicit” and“solicitation" mean and include any one or more of the following activities
conducted by an individual approved as a residential door-to-door solicitor:
1.Attempting or offering to sell or taking sales orders, for present or future delivery,
of any goods, merchandise or services of any kind, character or description, primarily for personal,
family orhousehold purposes;

2.Attempting or offering to sell or taking sales orders, for present or future delivery,
of books, magazines, periodicals, newspapers and every other type orkind of publication; or
3.Requesting directly or indirectly contributions on the plea or representation that
such contributions will be used for a charitable, educational or religious purpose; where any such
offer, taking, attempt or request is personally solicited or a sale of goods or services is
"Temporary or transient merchant” means all persons not having a permanent place of
business within the city who are engaged in selling or offering for sale any retail goods,
merchandise or services.Numerous temporary or transient merchants may be licensed under a
comprehensive license pursuant to an approved application.
“Temporary or transient merchant business license” means a license issued by the city
clerk in connection with a valid application as outlined in this chapter, and applies only to those
merchants who wish to sell or offer for sale retail goods, merchandise or services from fixed stands,
tables, booths, vehicles ortrailers at the location identified on the application orrenewal application
form.A transient business merchant license is only valid for a period of fourteen (14) consecutive
days beginning on the date of issuance.
5.76.030
Temporary or Transient Merchant -Comprehensive-License required--
Application.
A.
No person shall conduct business as a temporary or transient merchant within the
city unless:
1.The person has obtained a temporary or transient merchant business license from the
office of city clerk; or
2.The person is operating as a temporary or transient merchant pursuant to coverage
under a comprehensive license; or
3. The person meets one of the exemptions listed in Section 5.76.060 of this chapter.
B. Persons desiring a temporary or transient merchant business license, including an
annual comprehensive temporary or transient merchant license, must submit written application on
forms provided by the city clerk, together with payment of the licensing fee, to the office of city
clerk.Each application shallbe signed by the applicant in front ofa notary public and notarizedby
same.The licensing fee for a temporary or transient merchant license for a fourteen (14)
consecutive day period, or portion thereof, will be one hundred dollars ($100.00); the licensing fee
for an annual comprehensive temporary or transient merchant license will be three hundred dollars
($300.00)per year.Such application will include the following information, or any additional
information requested by the city clerk or chief of police, or their designee:
4
4:
1.Applicant's name, home address, telephone number and date of birth and, if
applicable, affiliated business or organization name, business physical and mailing address and
business telephone number.
2.Whether the applicant, or affiliated business or organization, has ever had a similar
type of business license, whether within Wyoming or elsewhere, revoked, suspended or denied.
3.Proposed date(s) of temporary or transient sales; hours of proposed sales; sales
address location and zoning classification, as defined by the Cheyenne Unified Development Code
(UDC), and description of the item(s) tobe sold.
4.If applicable, whether the applicant is authorized by the Wyoming Secretary of State
to dobusiness within the State of Wyoming, and whether the applicant has contacted the Wyoming
Department of Revenue and Taxation to acquire a state sales taxlicense.
5.Authorization for the city and its agents and employees to seek information and
conduct investigations of the applicant to verify that information contained upon the application is
true and correct.
6.Affirmation that the applicant agrees to comply fully with the rules and regulations
of the city governing the license requested and that the applicant further declares that the
information contained in the application is true and correct.
C.Upon receipt of an application and payment of the required license fee, the city clerk
will forward the application to the chief of police, or designee, for an applicant background review
and recommendation.The chief of police shall have the authority to recommend approval or
denial of any application for a temporary or transient merchant or comprehensive temporary or
transient merchant business license for the general health, safety and welfare of the community.
1.The chief of police may recommend the denial of any application that contains false,
misleading or incomplete information.The city clerk may require additional inspections and
approvals by other city agencies.
D.Every person licensed as a temporary or transient merchant, or comprehensive
temporary or transient merchant, must at all times possess and display such license in a conspicuous
place to the public while conducting sales pursuant to thelicense issued.

5.76.050Residential door-to-door solicitor restrictions-Prohibited practices.
A.No solicitor may solicit without wearing or displaying the assigned license
identification badge, as issued by the city clerk, to be viewable by the public at all times when
conducting door-to-door solicitation.Upon request by the public or any law enforcement officer,
proof of a current and valid residential door-to-door solicitors business license and license
identification badge shall be made available for inspection.No solicitor shall allow another
individual to use his or her assigned badge, and the badge shall not be worn or used for any other
purpose by the solicitor at times other than conducting door-to-door solicitation under the business
license.
B.No person shall engage in or conduct activities as a door-to-door solicitor upon any
residential premises without a prior invitation from the occupant or resident thereof if such
premises is posted or signed with a notice prominently displayed upon which is printed “No
Solicitors" or words of similar import. For the purposes of this subsection, residential premises
7
7:
willbe deemed to be posted against solicitation if the notice is exhibited on or near the main
entrance to the premises or on or near the main door to any residence located thereon.
C.No residential door-to-door business licensee or solicitor shall initiate solicitation
activities for potential customer services affiliated with installation of any equipment involving
electrical wiring, plumbing or remodeling any portion of a residential structure, without first
contacting the city's building safety department to determine whether a license or permit is
required.
D.No person will contact, engage in or conduct activities as a door-to-door solicitor
after having been asked by the owner or occupant thereof to leave the premises or residence.
E.No person shall solicit upon any residential premises, other than prior invitation by
the occupant or resident of the premises, prior to ten a.m. or after seven p.m., local time, of any day.
F.Not more than two door-to-door solicitors will engage in or conduct activities as a
solicitorat the same location and time for the samegoods, merchandise or services, or for religious
or charitable purposes.When conducting door-to-door solicitor activities, no solicitor will be
accompanied by an individual who has not been approved to receive a license identification badge.
Each individual in violation of this provision will be deemed to have violated such provision.
G.No solicitor shall, at the time ofinitial contact with a prospective customer or donor,
fail to verbally identify himself or herself and the business or company he or she represents, if
applicable, and the purpose of the solicitation.
H.No person engaged in or conducting activities as a door-to-door solicitor will
misrepresent the purpose of the solicitation or use any false, deceptive, misleading or untrue
information or practices, including any reference to orders placed by or sales entered into by other
residents or neighbors, to induce a sale, contribution, or placement of an order, or use any plan or
scheme which misrepresents the true purpose of the solicitation.
1.No door-to-door solicitor shall conduct solicitor activities in a disrespectful,
discourteous, aggressive, rude, offensive or inappropriate manner, including the use of abusive
resident.
J.No door-to-door solicitor shall finalize any sales or allow a customer to enter into or
sign any written agreement pertaining to the purchasing, delivery, including future deliveries from
orders taken, of any goods, merchandise or services without first verbally informing the potential
customer of any city licenses or permits that may be required as the result of the purchase, and that
the customer may have, pursuant to Wyoming law, three days in which to cancel the item(s) or
services purchased or ordered.

K.Nodoor-to-door solicitor shall make statements to potential customers or
contributors indicating or implying that the residential door-to-door solicitors business license or
license identification badgeissued by the cityclerk constitutes an endorsement bythe city of the

5.76.060Exemptions.
A.The following are exempt from the licensing provisions of this chapter:
1.Any person, as defined in Section 1.04.020 of city code, participating in fairs and
bazaars on public property when such fair or bazaar is sponsored or entirely operated by the city;
2.Any person participating in non-profit fund-raising activities, including religious,
educational and charitable activities, in which the items to be sold orraffled have been hand-crafted
or hand-made by local residents;
3. Charitable, non-profit and religious organizations and persons representing them;
provided, that the proceeds from sales are used only for charitable, non-profit or religious events
and purposes;
4.Any fund-raising sales by a recognized school or educational organization, where
profits solely benefit student members or a school/organization sponsored event.
5.Distribution of free literature or information which is not affiliated with any form of
attempting or offering to sell, or taking orders for present or future delivery, of anygoods,
merchandise or services, or that meets the definition of"solicit”".
5.76.070
License term.
A.Each initial annual comprehensive temporary or transient merchant business license
willbe effective for one yearfrom date ofissuance with a renewal application processed and license
issued as provided in this chapter and Chapter 5.04 of city code.Any change in location for an
annual comprehensive license will be pursuant to the requirements of Section5.04.070 of city code.
No change of ownership involving an annual comprehensive license is allowed.
B.Each temporary or transient merchant or residential door-to-door solicitors business
license will be effective for fourteen (14) consecutive days, or portion thereof.
C.Each license identification badge issued in affiliation with a residential door-to-door
solicitors business license will be effective for the same term as the business license.
D.Temporary or transient merchant and residential door-to-door solicitors business
licensees may submit application(s) for additional fourteen (14) consecutive day licenses by
6
9:
fulfilling the application requirements for an initial applicant under the provisions of this chapter.
5.76.080
Violations-Penalty.
A.
Any person who violates any provision of this chapter will be charged with a
misdemeanor, punishable pursuant to the general penalty provisions in Chapter 1.24 of city code.
Each violation will be deemed a separate offense.
B.Any person holding a valid temporary or transient merchant business license,
comprehensive license or residential door-to-door solicitors business license issued under this
chapter who violates any provision of this chapter will be subject to suspension or revocation
proceedings against the license as outlined within Chapter 5.04 of city code.
C.
Upon investigation and following determination that a door-to-door solicitor has
violated any portion of Section 5.76.050 outlined in this chapter, the chief of police shall have the
authority to revoke the individual's license identification badge and issue a citation.
1.No person charged with violating Section 5.76.050 (A) of this chapter shall be
convicted if he or she produces in court a valid residential door-to-door solicitors business license
and the license identification badge previously issued to him or her that was valid at the time the
citation was issued.
